decisions.reason: As a close-to-core delivery offering, it likely stays while management learns its demand and operational effects, though overlap with faster express options raises some risk of pruning.
The seventy-two-hour promise fits the firm's service strategy but is operationally demanding and margin-sensitive, so it faces the highest review risk if it falls short of aspiration levels.
A prominently launched, regulation-relevant fire-resistant exterior door is strongly aligned with the firm's capabilities and is likely to be retained unless early market feedback is clearly poor.
An express program across several door and gate models uses existing manufacturing and service resources well, making retention likely while the firm tests which variants perform best.
The digital ordering and service platform supports the firm's move toward deeper advisory and service integration, and a large firm with slack would usually give such an enabling platform more time.
A fire and smoke protection door is close to the established portfolio and addresses compliance-driven demand, so management would usually keep it unless results quickly disappoint.
